description: From transistors and gates to a working processor datapath. Every circuit is built, minimised, timed and tested in the browser lab until a small datapath runs.
modelledOn: Harris and Harris, Digital Design and Computer Architecture
Nand2Tetris: Building a Modern Computer from First Principles (hardware part)
outcomes: Convert between number systems and codes, and reason about overflow and signed arithmetic.
Specify, minimise and implement any combinational function with gates, muxes or ROM/PLA.
Analyse and design synchronous sequential circuits with flip-flops and finite state machines.
Reason about timing: propagation delay, setup and hold, clock period and glitches.
Build arithmetic units, registers and memories, and compose them into a simple datapath.

units.title: Digital abstraction and number representation
topics: Why digital: noise margins, the static discipline, voltage levels for 0 and 1
Binary, octal, hexadecimal; base conversion; fixed-point fractions
Signed numbers: sign-magnitude, one's and two's complement; overflow detection
Codes: BCD, Gray code, ASCII and Unicode; unit-distance codes
Error detection and correction: parity, checksums, Hamming distance and Hamming(7,4)

units.title: Boolean algebra and logic gates
topics: Axioms and theorems of Boolean algebra; duality; De Morgan's laws
Switching functions; truth tables; canonical sum-of-products and product-of-sums
Gate families: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR; universal gates
CMOS implementation of inverters and NAND gates; fan-in, fan-out, propagation delay
Logic families compared: TTL, CMOS; voltage levels and power

units.title: Minimisation and multilevel implementation
topics: Algebraic simplification
Karnaugh maps for 2 to 5 variables; prime implicants, essential prime implicants, don't cares
Quine-McCluskey tabular method and the covering problem
Two-level versus multilevel logic; NAND-only and NOR-only realisations
Hazards and glitches; hazard-free design

units.title: Combinational building blocks
topics: Design procedure: specification, truth table, minimisation, implementation, verification
Half and full adders, ripple-carry adders, carry-lookahead and carry-select adders
Subtractors and two's-complement add/subtract units; comparators
Multipliers: array multiplier and shift-and-add
Multiplexers, demultiplexers, encoders, priority encoders, decoders, code converters
Implementing functions with multiplexers and decoders; tri-state buffers and buses

units.title: Latches, flip-flops and timing
topics: The bistable element; SR latch; gated D latch
Edge-triggered D flip-flop; master-slave construction; JK and T flip-flops
Characteristic and excitation tables; converting one flip-flop type to another
Timing: setup time, hold time, clock-to-Q, minimum clock period, metastability
Asynchronous inputs, synchronisers and debouncing

units.title: Sequential circuits and finite state machines
topics: Registers, shift registers (SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO), ring and Johnson counters
Synchronous and asynchronous (ripple) counters; up/down and modulo-N counters
Moore and Mealy machines; state diagrams and state tables
FSM design procedure: state assignment, next-state logic, output logic
State reduction and equivalent states; one-hot encoding
Worked designs: sequence detector, vending machine, traffic-light controller

units.title: Memory and programmable logic
topics: Memory organisation: address, data, word size; read and write cycles
ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash; SRAM and DRAM cells; refresh
Implementing combinational logic with ROM
PLA, PAL and the idea of programmable interconnect; introduction to FPGAs
Register files and simple RAM built from flip-flops

units.title: From logic to a datapath
topics: Arithmetic logic unit: operation select, flags (zero, carry, overflow, negative)
Register transfer notation and control signals
A minimal datapath: registers, ALU, memory, program counter
Instruction execution as a sequence of register transfers (bridge to Computer Organisation and Architecture)

schedule.title: Digital abstraction and number systems
schedule.exercise: Convert twelve values between binary, octal, hexadecimal and decimal, and represent six numbers in 8-bit two's complement, marking which additions overflow.

tasks.title: Convert 10 decimal values to binary, octal and hex with the base converter and check each step by converting back
Represent 12 and -12 in 8-bit sign-magnitude, one's and two's complement, then add pairs of values and flag every overflow case
Drive an inverter with a ramp input in the circuit bench, measure the noise margins from the transfer curve, and judge if a 0.4 V noise spike is safe

schedule.title: Codes and error control
schedule.exercise: Encode the digits of a Ghana phone number in BCD, write the 3-bit Gray code sequence, and encode and correct a single-bit error in a Hamming(7,4) word.

tasks.title: Convert the decimal numbers 0 to 15 into binary, BCD and 4-bit Gray code and tabulate where successive Gray codes differ in one bit
Build an even parity generator and checker for 4 data bits from XOR gates and verify all 16 inputs flag a single injected bit error
Build a Hamming(7,4) encoder and single-error corrector from gates, then inject each of the seven possible bit errors and verify correct output

schedule.title: Boolean algebra, gates and logic families
schedule.exercise: Prove De Morgan's laws with truth tables, write a function in canonical sum-of-products and product-of-sums, and explain why NAND alone is enough to build any circuit.

tasks.title: Build the circuit for a given 3-variable function from AND, OR and NOT gates and check its truth table against the specification
Rebuild AND, OR, NOT and XOR using only NAND gates and prove each against the reference gate for all input combinations
Build a CMOS NAND gate from transistors, measure its propagation delay with a load of increasing fan-out, and chart delay against fan-out

schedule.title: Minimisation with K-maps and tabular methods
schedule.exercise: Minimise two four-variable functions with don't cares using Karnaugh maps, then confirm one of them with the Quine-McCluskey tabular method.

tasks.title: Fill a 4-variable Karnaugh map from a given truth table, group the ones, and write the minimal sum-of-products expression
Minimise a 4-input function with three don't cares using a K-map, build it, and verify against the original truth table
Implement Quine-McCluskey for up to five variables, run it on a given function, and compare its answer with your hand K-map result

schedule.title: Multilevel logic and hazards
schedule.exercise: Convert a minimal two-level expression to a NAND-only network, then find the static-1 hazard in a given circuit and add a redundant term to remove it.

tasks.title: Convert a given AND-OR circuit to NAND-only form in the bench and verify that the truth table is unchanged
Build a given circuit with unequal gate delays, apply a single input change, and capture the glitch on the output in the timing view
Remove the static-1 hazard from a multiplexer circuit by adding a consensus term, and show the clean waveform before and after

schedule.title: Adders, subtractors and comparators
schedule.exercise: Derive the full-adder equations from its truth table, estimate the worst-case delay of a 4-bit ripple-carry adder, and explain how carry-lookahead shortens it.

tasks.title: Build a full adder from two half adders and an OR gate and verify its eight input cases in the truth table
Build a 4-bit ripple-carry adder from full adders and verify all 512 input cases in the truth table
Build a 4-bit add/subtract unit with overflow flag using XOR gates, and test positive, negative and overflow cases in two's complement

schedule.title: Multipliers, multiplexers and decoders
schedule.exercise: Implement a 3-input function with an 8-to-1 multiplexer and again with a 3-to-8 decoder and OR gate, and trace a 3x3 array multiplier on one input pair.

tasks.title: Build a 2-to-4 decoder from gates and verify one output goes high for each of the four input combinations
Implement a given 3-variable function using a 4-to-1 multiplexer with one variable as data input, and verify the full truth table
Build a 2x2 array multiplier and a 4x4 version from AND gates and adders, and verify 20 products including 15x15

schedule.title: Latches and flip-flops
schedule.exercise: Fill in characteristic and excitation tables for D, JK and T flip-flops, and show how to build a T flip-flop from a D flip-flop.

tasks.title: Build an SR latch from two NOR gates, step through set, reset, hold and the forbidden input, and record each output state
Build a master-slave D flip-flop from two gated latches and show in the timing view that the output changes only at the clock edge
Convert a D flip-flop into JK and T behaviour using extra gates, and verify each against its characteristic table over a clocked test sequence

schedule.title: Timing and asynchronous inputs
schedule.exercise: Given setup, hold and clock-to-Q times, compute the minimum clock period and maximum frequency for a two-stage register path, and explain how a two-flip-flop synchroniser reduces metastability.

tasks.title: Measure clock-to-Q delay of a flip-flop in the timing view and compare it with the datasheet value given in the task
Raise the clock frequency on a two-register path until a setup violation appears, and report the minimum period against your calculation
Debounce a bouncing push-button signal with an SR latch and with a two-flip-flop synchroniser, and compare the clean outputs in the timing view

schedule.title: Registers, counters and state machines
schedule.exercise: Draw the state diagram and table for a mod-6 counter, then convert the same behaviour into a Moore machine and a Mealy machine with an enable input.

tasks.title: Build a 4-bit shift register from D flip-flops, load a pattern serially, and record the contents after each of four clock pulses
Build a synchronous mod-10 up counter with reset and verify it cycles 0 to 9 on the timing diagram
Design a 3-bit up/down counter with enable and verify direction changes mid-count produce the correct sequence over 20 clock cycles

schedule.title: Finite state machine design
schedule.exercise: Design a sequence detector for 1011 with overlap as a Mealy machine, then reduce a given 6-state table to its minimum number of states.

tasks.title: Implement a given 4-state Moore machine with flip-flops and gates, and verify its outputs against the state table over a test sequence
Design a 1011 sequence detector with overlap, build it, and test it on a 24-bit input stream containing four occurrences
Design a traffic-light controller for a two-way junction with a pedestrian button, compare binary and one-hot state encoding, and verify the timing

schedule.title: Memory and programmable logic
schedule.exercise: Size the address and data lines for a 4K x 8 memory, implement a 3-bit squarer using a ROM table, and explain what the DRAM refresh requirement costs.

tasks.title: Write four values into a small RAM in the bench, read them back, and record the address, data and write-enable signals for each cycle
Implement a 3-bit squaring function using a ROM and fill in its contents, then verify all eight inputs
Build a 4 x 4-bit register file from flip-flops with two read ports and one write port, and test simultaneous read and write

schedule.title: ALU and a minimal datapath
schedule.exercise: List the register transfers and control signals needed to execute ADD R1, R2 on a minimal datapath, and write the control word for each clock step.

tasks.title: Build a 4-bit ALU supporting AND, OR, ADD and SUB with a 2-bit select, and verify the zero and carry flags on eight test pairs
Connect registers, the ALU and a program counter into a simple datapath and execute a three-step register transfer by hand-set controls
Trace a four-instruction assembly program on the CPU visualiser, listing the register transfers and control signals active in each fetch and execute step
